title: Uses of Earth Materials by People

competencies.text: Describe properties and local availability of rocks, minerals, and soils. Explain how they are harnessed for industries.

days.title: Minerals, Rocks and Soils
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

This week you will describe the properties and local availability of rocks, minerals and soils and explain how they are harnessed for industries.

💎 Three Earth Materials

MaterialDefinitionExamples
MineralNaturally occurring, inorganic solid with a definite chemical composition and crystal structureQuartz, calcite, gold, copper minerals
RockNatural solid made of one or more mineralsGranite, limestone, basalt
SoilLoose mixture of weathered rock, organic matter, water and airSand, silt, clay, loam

🔍 Identifying Minerals

  • Hardness — resistance to scratching, on the Mohs scale from 1 (talc) to 10 (diamond).
  • Streak — color of the powder when rubbed on a tile; more reliable than surface color.
  • Luster — how it reflects light: metallic, glassy, dull.
  • Cleavage/fracture — breaks along flat planes or irregularly.
  • Density — gold feels much heavier than quartz of the same size.
  • Acid test — calcite (in limestone) fizzes in dilute acid, releasing CO₂.

✅ Quick Check

3 questions — read each explanation.

scenario.text: What is the difference between a mineral and a rock?

choices.label: A rock is made of one or more minerals
A mineral is made of many different rocks
Rocks are always softer than any mineral
Minerals are only found in volcanoes

scenario.explanation: Minerals are the building blocks; rocks are aggregates of one or more minerals.

scenario.text: A mineral scratches glass but is scratched by quartz. Which property is being tested?
scenario.explanation: Scratch tests compare hardness using the Mohs scale.

scenario.text: A rock fizzes when a drop of dilute acid is placed on it. Which mineral does it most likely contain?
scenario.explanation: Calcite (calcium carbonate) reacts with acid to release CO₂ bubbles; limestone and marble contain calcite.

days.title: The Rock Cycle
days.content:
🪨 Three Rock Types

TypeHow it formsExamples and uses
IgneousMagma or lava cools and hardensBasalt (road gravel), granite (countertops), pumice (scrubbing)
SedimentarySediments are deposited, compacted and cemented; or minerals precipitateLimestone (cement), sandstone, shale, coal
MetamorphicExisting rock changed by heat and pressure without meltingMarble from limestone (Romblon tiles), slate from shale

🔄 The Rock Cycle

Rocks constantly change from one type to another. Weathering and erosion break rocks into sediments; sediments become sedimentary rock; heat and pressure turn rocks into metamorphic rock; melting creates magma that cools into igneous rock. In the Philippines, active volcanoes, uplift and heavy tropical rain keep this cycle moving quickly.

🌋 Cooling Speed Matters

Magma that cools slowly underground forms large crystals (granite). Lava that cools quickly at the surface forms small crystals (basalt) or even glass (obsidian). Gas bubbles trapped in fast-cooling lava make pumice, light enough to float.

🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each term to its description. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

match.right: Natural inorganic solid with a definite composition
match.why: It has an ordered crystal structure.

match.right: Forms when magma or lava cools
Changed by heat and pressure without melting
Used for tiles, sculptures and flooring

match.why: Gas bubbles were trapped as lava cooled.

days.title: Philippine Earth Resources
days.content:
⛏️ Mineral Wealth

Because of its volcanic and tectonic history, the Philippines is rich in metallic and non-metallic resources.

ResourceWhere found (examples)Main uses
GoldBenguet, Masbate, Davao de OroJewelry, electronics, reserves
CopperBenguet, Cebu (Toledo), ZambalesElectric wiring, plumbing, electronics
NickelSurigao, Palawan, ZambalesStainless steel, batteries
ChromiteZambalesStainless steel, chrome plating
LimestoneRizal, Cebu, BoholCement, lime, building stone
MarbleRomblonTiles, sculpture
ClayMany lowland areas (e.g., Ilocos)Bricks, pottery (burnay jars)

🌱 Soils

Sandy soil drains fast and holds few nutrients; clay holds water and nutrients but can become waterlogged and hard; loam, a balanced mix of sand, silt and clay with organic matter, is best for most crops. Volcanic soils are especially fertile.

⚖️ Costs of Extraction

Mining and quarrying bring jobs and materials but can cause deforestation, erosion, silted rivers and acid mine drainage. The Philippine Mining Act (RA 7942) requires environmental permits and rehabilitation of mined land.

🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Apply your knowledge of earth materials. Read every explanation. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

scenario.text: A construction firm needs cement for a bridge. Which earth material is the MAIN raw material?
scenario.explanation: Cement is made by heating limestone (calcium carbonate) with clay.

scenario.text: A farmer's soil drains very fast and her crops lack nutrients. What should she do?

choices.label: Mix in compost so it holds water and nutrients
Add more sand so the water drains away even faster
Remove all organic matter from the top layer
Pave the field so the soil cannot dry out

scenario.explanation: Sandy soil drains quickly. Adding organic matter moves it toward loam, which holds water and nutrients better.

scenario.text: A copper mine opens upstream of a farming town. Which impact should the town watch for MOST closely?

choices.label: Rivers becoming much colder in summer
Copper turning all the rice crops into gold
More rain falling only on the mine site

scenario.explanation: Exposed sulfide rocks can produce acid mine drainage that carries toxic metals into water used for farms and drinking.

scenario.text: Why does granite have large crystals while basalt has tiny ones?

choices.label: Basalt cooled slowly deep inside the Earth
Granite formed from sediments in the sea
Basalt was squeezed by heat and pressure

scenario.explanation: Slow cooling deep underground gives crystals time to grow large; fast cooling at the surface makes small crystals.

scenario.text: A potter in Vigan makes burnay jars. Why is clay the best soil for this?

choices.label: Its fine, sticky particles hold a shape
It drains water quickly and stays loose and dry
It is full of large rocks and pebbles
It contains much more sand than silt

scenario.explanation: Clay's very fine particles stick together when wet and hold a shape, then harden when fired.

days.title: Using Earth Materials Responsibly
days.content:
♻️ Non-Renewable Resources

Minerals and rocks form over millions of years, so on a human time scale they are non-renewable. Using them wisely means:

  • Recycling metals — recycling copper and aluminum uses far less energy than mining new ore.
  • Responsible mining — permits, water treatment, tailings management and replanting mined areas.
  • Protecting soil — terracing, cover crops and reforestation reduce erosion; topsoil can take centuries to form.
  • Small-scale miners' safety — mercury used to extract gold is toxic to people and rivers; safer methods exist.

📱 Earth Materials in Your Phone

A smartphone contains copper (wiring), gold (connectors), nickel and cobalt (battery), silicon from quartz (chips) and many other elements. Every device links us to mines somewhere — and recycling old phones recovers these materials.

🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Lab

3 lives, 6 keys. You need 70% (5 of 6). Read each explanation.

choices.label: By cooling of magma or lava
By heat and pressure without melting
By evaporation of salt water at sea

escape.explanation: Igneous rocks form when molten rock (magma underground, lava at the surface) cools and solidifies.

escape.text: Which rock type forms when heat and pressure change existing rock?
escape.explanation: Metamorphic rocks form from existing rocks transformed by heat and pressure, like limestone becoming marble.

escape.text: Which soil type is BEST for most crops?
escape.explanation: Loam balances drainage and water-holding and contains organic matter.

escape.text: Which Philippine province is famous for marble?
escape.explanation: Romblon is known nationwide for its marble industry.

escape.text: Which metal from Surigao and Palawan is used in stainless steel and batteries?
escape.explanation: The Philippines is a major nickel ore producer; nickel is used in stainless steel and batteries.

choices.label: They form over millions of years
They regrow during each rainy season
They can be grown in farms
They are made fresh by plants

escape.explanation: Mineral deposits take geological time to form, far longer than human lifetimes.
